title: Throttle Fade Controller and Anticipatory Offset Orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce Throttle Fade Controller: gradual decay of tenant-level throttles with anticipatory offsets to reduce hard cutoffs during transient demand drops. New telemetry metrics and operator flags. Backwards compatible; opt-in via operator config.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently apply abrupt tenant throttles when utilization crosses hard thresholds which causes short-lived request loss and poor tail latency for bursty tenants. This PR adds a Throttle Fade Controller that replaces instant hard-throttle transitions with a controlled exponential decay (fade) and pairs it with an Anticipatory Offset Orchestrator that nudges per-tenant headroom ahead of predicted demand drops using a short-term demand slope detector. The goal is to preserve throughput guarantees while reducing churn/evictions during noisy signals.Technical summary: 1) New controller pkg/autoscaler/throttle_fade_controller.go implements a per-tenant state machine that tracks throttle_level, last_scale_time, fade_factor, and a hold window. Throttles are decayed using an exponential schedule tuned by operator-configurable fade_half_life and min_floor. 2) The anticipatory orchestrator (pkg/autoscaler/anticipatory_offset.go) computes a 30s and 5min slope on admitted requests and emits an anticipatory_offset_gain per tenant which temporarily increases the soft headroom budget to avoid over-aggressive decommit. 3) Telemetry: new metrics decayed_throttle_rate, anticipatory_offset_gain, request_slope_30s and request_slope_5m are registered in observability/metrics_registry.yaml and emitted via pkg/telemetry/metrics_collector.go. 4) Operator config flags and a values.yaml snippet allow ops to opt in and tune behavior (deploy/dedicated/operator/values.yaml and pkg/cli/operator_flags.go). 5) A conservative rollout path: controller is off by default; can be enabled per-pool; includes canary policy changes for 10% of traffic implemented in pkg/rollout/canary_policy.go.Rollout and safety: default fade_half_life is large (30s) and min_floor = 0.05 to avoid starving tenants. There is an automatic safety circuit that reverts to previous hard-throttle if the controller observes sustained SLA violations (pkg/autoscaler/safety_circuit.go). Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for the decay math and slope detector in test/unit/throttle_fade_unit_test.go; an integration test that replays real production traces with synthetic bursts in test/integration/throttle_fade_test.go; benchmark harness in benchmark-lab/benchmarks/throttle_fade_bench.go. Docs: a short design doc and operator guidance added to docs/dedicated/throttle-fade.md and examples/dedicated/anticipatory-offset-config.yaml.Migration notes: feature is opt-in, no DB schema changes. Operator operators should enable on a small pool and observe decayed_throttle_rate and request_slope metrics before broad rollout.Checklist: [x] design review (ENG-2142) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] telemetry registered [x] operator flags [x] docs and example config [x] canary rollout policy [x] perf benchmark. Related: references ENG-2190 for fairness constraints and SUP-341 for a customer incident motivating smoother throttles.

summary: Adds a gradual throttle decay controller and anticipatory headroom offset to reduce abrupt throttling and improve tail behavior for bursty tenants. Opt-in operator config, telemetry, tests, docs, and canary rollout included.
notes_for_ops: Default disabled. To enable: set dedicated.operator.throttleFade.enabled=true and tune fade_half_life, cooldown_multiplier, and min_floor. Watch decayed_throttle_rate, anticipatory_offset_gain, request_slope_30s, and request_slope_5m. Enable on a small canary pool first.
impact_assessment: Low-risk opt-in change. No client-visible API changes. Risk is potential under-throttling in pathological high-slope scenarios; mitigated by safety_circuit that reverts to hard-throttle when SLA regressions exceed configured thresholds.
